textbookBox.concept: A chemical reaction changes substances into new ones. Signs include a change in state, colour, temperature, or the evolution of a gas.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A chemical reaction changes substances into new ones. Signs include a change in state, colour, temperature, or the evolution of a gas.
beats.speakEn: A chemical reaction changes substances into new ones. Signs include a change in state, colour, temperature, or the evolution of a gas.

beats.en: We write a word equation first: magnesium + oxygen gives magnesium oxide. Reactants are on the left and products on the right.
beats.speakEn: We write a word equation first: magnesium + oxygen gives magnesium oxide. Reactants are on the left and products on the right.

textbookBox.concept: A skeletal equation uses formulae: Mg + O2 gives MgO. It is not balanced because oxygen atoms are 2 on the left and 1 on the right.

beats.en: A skeletal equation uses formulae: Mg + O2 gives MgO. It is not balanced because oxygen atoms are 2 on the left and 1 on the right.
beats.speakEn: A skeletal equation uses formulae: Mg + O2 gives MgO. It is not balanced because oxygen atoms are 2 on the left and 1 on the right.

beats.en: The law of conservation of mass says that mass is neither created nor destroyed, so the number of atoms of each element must be the same on both sides.
beats.speakEn: The law of conservation of mass says that mass is neither created nor destroyed, so the number of atoms of each element must be the same on both sides.
